title: Request heap + hypothesis lab — Nov 2029
content:
Purpose/context:
Quick dump from the "hypothesis lab" session (11/12–11/19). This is intentionally messy: a single place to park raw asks, first-cut hypotheses about causes, and tiny experiment ideas we can run in the next sprint. Goal: turn 20–30 minutes of field noise into 3 prioritized probes.

Summary (toplines):
- Recurring themes: (1) unexpected latency spikes when using multi-turn chat with custom tool-calls, (2) customers asking for clearer per-request cost attribution for caching/batching-induced token savings, (3) confusion about model fallback behavior in Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Several mid-enterprise customers report drop-offs after test (P0/P1) because of unpredictable billing jumps when enabling caching. They like the performance but can't forecast month-to-month.
- Many asks are small surface fixes (UI/label + docs) that would reduce CS load quickly.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim where available):
- "We turned on prefix caching and our bill halved overnight — but the dashboard still shows the same token numbers. How do we map billing to cache hits?" — Fintech POC (NDA).
- "When the Canary falls back to smaller model we see 500ms blips then a big spike — hard to debug in Prod" — Retail AI platform.
- "SDK 2.3 changed the streaming hook and our internal UI broke; the docs didn't call out the breaking default" — Integration partner.

Raw requests (heap, unfiltered):
- 'per-request cache hit metric in API response' (ask from 3 customers) — currently surfaced only in Console logs.
- 'predictive bill estimator when turning on Dedicated caching' — want delta pre/post.
- 'explicit indicator when fallback to compatible model happens' — user wants to see reason (region/capacity/latency/cost).
- 'per-route token accounting for shared workloads' — teams share single API key and want route-level cost splits.
- 'granular streaming hooks example' — expand SDK examples to include resumed streams + error handling.
- 'simple rollback button in console for rollouts' — non-engineering PM wants 1-click revert.

Hypotheses about root causes (1–2 lines each):
- Visibility gaps: Console shows aggregate tokens but not adjusted-for-cache numbers; customers equate tokens -> dollars. We don't clearly show cache hit rate impact on bill.
- Fallback telemetry: The runtime emits fallback events but not mapped to the customer-facing route; SRE traces exist but UI/SDK don't correlate.
- Docs drift: SDK changes outpaced examples; streaming API edge cases (resuming + function-calls) not covered.

Micro-probes / experiments (quick, low-cost):
1) Add "cache_hit_rate" field to the per-request debugging header (not billing) and run a 2-week opt-in for 5 customers. Measure CS tickets and billing variance. (Owner: Marcus; Jira: CS-3421)
2) Console UX: Add a "billing delta" quick card in Rollouts page that simulates cost impact for enabling caching on a route (calculation based on recent 7/30 day token & cache hit estimates). Launch as beta for Dedicated customers. (Owner: Ava; Epic: PRODOPT-88)
3) Small docs/SDK push: Expand Streaming hooks section with a "resilient resume" recipe + one PR in SDK (target: patch release 2.3.1). (Owner: Sofia; PR: platform/pull/1498)
4) Alert prototype: Surface fallback reason code (region/capacity/compatibility) in request tracing UI; add an opt-in trace view for customers to see detail. Run with 2 enterprise customers. (Owner: Liam)

Prioritization note (quick scoring):
- Impact (customer pain + churn risk): per-request cache visibility (9/10); fallback visibility (8/10); SDK docs (5/10); per-route cost split (6/10 but high complexity).
- Effort (engineering + UX): SDK/docs (low), per-request header (low–med), console billing delta card (med), per-route split (high).
- Quick wins: SDK/docs patch, add debug header, small console card mock.

Open questions / things to validate with PMs/Eng: 
- Does adding cache_hit_rate to responses have privacy/market implications? (legal/security check).
- Can runtime expose fallback rationales cheaply or do we need a longer tracing affordance?
- Is per-route accounting possible with current API key semantics (or do we require separate keys/labels)?

Action items (next 10 days):
- Marcus: prototype response-debug header + minimal server flag to opt-in (deadline 11/26). Attach quick curl examples for CS. (linked to CS-3421)
- Ava + Product: sketch the billing delta card mock and gather 3 Dedicated accounts for beta (deadline 11/27).
- Sofia: open SDK PR for streaming-resume recipe; include a unit test and an example app snippet (deadline 11/24).
- Liam: scope a small trace-surface spike with SRE to see if fallback reasons are already captured; produce a one-slide summary for Eng sync (deadline 11/25).

Risks and guardrails: 
- Billing delta card could be misinterpreted as exact; label clearly as estimate and include link to docs.
- Sending per-request debug fields to customer logs may expose internal routing reasons — coordinate with Security.

Notes from CS calls (raw):
- 11/13 call — Retail AI platform: losing users after Canary; accepted to try a card-level "why did we fallback" in the console.
- 11/14 call — Fintech: excited about caching but wants a monthly estimate so finance can budget.
- 11/16 email — Partner: SDK example broke on resume; offered to test the patch.

Potential - tiny product concepts (brainstorm):
- "Cost simulator" inside Route settings: slider for cache hit rates and model quantization to instantly preview monthly spend.
- "Fallback annotations" — inline annotations in trace viewer linking to recommended mitigations (increase pool, change region, bump fallback model).
- "Billing snapshot" export (CSV) showing gross tokens, cache-saved tokens, and net estimated charge per route.

Discussion log / thought fragments (notes-to-self):
- If we can reduce one billing churn case per quarter that's >$100k ARR saved (estimate from AE). Need to validate.
- Some customers treat token -> $ mapping rigidly; educating them + showing delta might be easiest path.
- Worth making a small 'migration checklist' doc for customers moving from Hosted -> Dedicated with precise hooks: what metrics change, expected bill variance, default fallback behavior.

References / useful threads:
- Confluence draft: "Dedicated migration checklist" (internal) — link above.
- Slack: #cs-signals — thread on caching economics (11/12—11/19).
- GitHub: streaming resume example PR (1498).

Immediate asks for Eng/Product review:
- Can Eng confirm cost/infra risk of exposing cache_hit_rate on responses?
- PM: prioritize a small UX mock for billing delta — we can validate with 3 accounts quickly.

TL;DR: We have a cluster of related customer pain around "visibility" (billing, fallback, streaming behavior). There are 3 low-effort experiments (debug header, SDK docs patch, billing-delta card) that together should reduce support load and lower churn risk. If this looks right, I'll convert top 3 probes into scoped tickets and assign owners.

-- end of dump --
